title: Intern, Corporate Governance (6 Months)

As an Intern, Corporate Governance Team, you will gain hands-on experience in administrative support, project coordination, stakeholder management, and executive operations, making this an excellent opportunity to develop critical business and organizational skills in a fast-paced environment. In this role you will: Administrative & Financial Support: Assist in processing expense reports, purchase orders, and managing incoming correspondence for the Executive Office. Travel & Logistics Coordination: Support travel arrangements, including research and bookings for flights, hotels, and team activities. Meeting & Event Preparation: Prepare meeting materials, presentations, and agendas for high-level executive sessions. Project Coordination: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to track deadlines, follow up on deliverables, and support Executive Office initiatives. Ad-Hoc Support: Assist with special projects and additional tasks as required by the Executive Office team. Proficiency in Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides) is an advantage. A proactive, problem-solving mindset with a strong sense of ownership. Ability to maintain confidentiality and discretion in handling sensitive information. Based in Berlin or willing to relocate for the duration of the internship. What’s in it for you: Accelerate your career growth by joining one of Europe’s most talked about disruptors Employee benefits include discounts to fitness & wellness memberships, language courses, public transportation and more. A high degree of autonomy and access to cutting edge technologies - all while working with a friendly team of peers of diverse nationalities, life experiences and backgrounds. We've eliminated physical branches, paperwork, and hidden fees for an elegant digital experience and supreme savings. Giving people the power to live and bank their way is what gets us out of bed in the morning and inspires the work that we do. We are headquartered in Berlin with offices in multiple cities across Europe, including Madrid and Barcelona, and a 1,700-strong team of more than 80 nationalities. Equal opportunities for all At N26, we believe our strength lies in our people and the varied perspectives they bring. We strive to build diverse teams that drive innovation and business success. title: Human Factors Project Manager (m/f/d) (part-time contractor, 3-month review)
description: About Hilo by Aktiia High blood pressure is the world's most common disease, causing 18M deaths each year. At Hilo by Aktiia, we're building a world where no lives are lost to its effects — with technology that helps people take control of their health. We're a venture-backed scale-up with $96M raised from investors in Europe and the US. Rooted in 18 years of research at the Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology (CSEM), our device is the world's only medically accurate, cuffless, continuous blood pressure monitor for daily use — clinically validated and CE Marked as a Class IIa medical device, now available in 12 countries. In July, we launched in the US. We're a remote-first company headquartered in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, united by our passion for impact and innovation. Applicants must already hold a valid visa or work permit for their country of residence, as Hilo is not able to provide visa sponsorship. About the role Hilo is looking for an experienced Human Factors Project Manager to own all of our human factors and usability work. Right now that work is split across Product, Design, Clinical Operations, QARA and outside agencies, and no single person is accountable for it. You'll be that person. You'll coordinate the specialists, keep work moving between teams and make sure every deliverable meets the quality and regulatory standard. That frees our domain teams to get back to their own work. What you'll own Usability studies: You'll own the study calendar, protocols and relationships with external labs such as Sage Research. This covers formative and summative studies across hardware and software, including FDA submission work for Hilo Medical. You'll make sure findings get back to design on a regular schedule. IFU and Quick Start Guide: You'll decide what content goes in the QSG, the app and the IFU. You'll also own version control and localisation (Phrase, Novalins) and brief and manage freelance designers and print partners. Packaging: You'll own packaging briefs from start to finish and coordinate agencies (ARD, Superhuit, Carac Design) and freelance packaging designers. You'll keep the work aligned with regulatory, cost and manufacturing constraints. Clinical studies: You'll connect the human factors evidence from ClinOps-run trials with the human factors evidence for the product we ship to customers. Roadmap and reporting: You'll keep a single human factors roadmap and manage dependencies, resourcing and budgets across teams. Each month you'll report confidence levels and raise any risks to leadership. This is a part time contractor role of up to three days per week, with a total fee of CHF 17,500 for the initial engagement. We would like to start as soon as possible, with a review after three months. Requirements What you'll bring Human factors or usability engineering experience in medical devices, ideally with wearables or connected health Proven project or programme management: you've owned the plan, sequenced multiple workstreams and delivered on deadlines through others Hands-on knowledge of IEC 62366 usability engineering, use-related risk documentation (e.g. UFMEAs) and IFU development Experience managing agencies, labs and freelancers Clear, confident communication, with a track record of connecting Product, Clinical and Quality/Regulatory teams First priorities Audit of our current processes and human factors function Set up the usability study calendar Get a decision on the content split for the QSG "5-minute sheet" redesign Nice to have: FDA submission experience, a UX research background, and familiarity with InDesign/Figma localisation workflows Benefits At Hilo by Aktiia, our values guide everything we do: Move the Needle — You focus on what drives real impact. Move Fast, Learn, Refine — You work with urgency and purpose, balancing speed with quality. You treat feedback as a chance to learn, and you're deep in customer and partner feedback — translating it to action quickly. Team First — You collaborate effectively across teams and build trust through clarity and respect.
